title: Observability ingestion gateway and smart-route for SLO fidelity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight ingest gateway service that normalizes incoming traces/metrics/logs, attaches SLO-context metadata, and performs smart routing and adaptive sampling so that downstream SLO evaluation pipelines retain fidelity for high-risk tenants without overwhelming storage/processing budgets.
background: We currently receive traces and metrics from multiple collectors with inconsistent span tags and sampling behavior. SLO evaluation and burn-rate alerts miss signal for a subset of noisy tenants and overconsume for low-risk workloads. This ticket consolidates an ingestion-time point to: 1) canonicalize span labels, 2) perform SLO-aware adaptive span sampling, and 3) route enriched telemetry to tiered pipelines (hot path for SLO-critical, cold for analytics).
proposed_solution: Introduce an Observability Ingestion Gateway (OIG) deployed as a scalable service in the observability fleet. Key features: canonicalizer transforms (map legacy span keys to canonical keys), tenant-level SLO tags propagated from request metadata, adaptive span sampler (ruleset that increases sampling when tenant burn-rate nears threshold or when error/latency spikes), and smart router that sends enriched data to one of three pipelines: realtime-slo, standard-metrics, longterm-archive. Add hooks so tracing libraries can set SLO-context headers. Provide a small SDK shim and config knobs for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) OIG accepts traces and emits canonicalized spans with _slo_context set for >95% of ingested requests in staging.
2) Adaptive sampler increases retention for tenants with simulated burn-rate >0.7 and reduces baseline sampling for low-risk tenants in controlled rollout.
3) Realtime-slo pipeline latency stays under 2s P95 for evaluation windows after OIG integration.
4) End-to-end SLO alerting (burn-rate & latency) fires for injected anomalies in test tenants and does not double-fire due to duplicate spans.
5) Console dashboard shows per-tenant ingestion tier and sample-rate over time.
6) Migration plan documented for removing legacy collectors and a rollback path tested.
milestones: 2026-03-10: implement adaptive sampler + routing to realtime-slo pipeline
2026-03-18: integration tests with SLO evaluator and synthetic workloads
risks: Risk of increased ingest cost if adaptive sampling is miscalibrated; risk of false positives from aggressive routing; potential backwards-compatibility issues for customers that rely on raw span tags. Need to ensure OIG is horizontally scalable and fault-tolerant (fallback to pass-through mode).
notes: We will reuse parts of the canonical tag map from the trace-enrichment library and extend it for model-version, customer_tier, and route_group. Consider implementing a cheap ML-based anomaly scorer in a follow-up (ENG-92500). Coordinate with privacy/compliance for PII in span attributes.
